claims.text: Design review trade-off point 'where search runs': inside PostgreSQL nothing new to run and no copy, but searches share the database with order placement.

Review point 'whole-word matching': no misspelt words, no synonyms, accepted until ADR 0030's revisit condition. Its gain: unaccented typing finds products (driver 1) with PostgreSQL's own normalisation; misspellings/synonyms were the engine's offer.

Under ADR 0030's rule a query word matches only a whole normalised word of the name, and the design review's example needs every query word to match; phm is not phim, ngh is not nghe, so 'ban phm' and 'tai ngh' find nothing.
claims.source_hint: ADR 0030 @ stage-4 lines 34-41; product-search-design-review.md lines 41-43; PostgreSQL 17 docs 12.3.2 Parsing Queries, 12.6.2 Simple Dictionary

claims.text: ADR 0030 revisit condition: misspelling or synonym complaints above 5% of search feedback in a month (assumed), or search load above headroom even on the replica. The product owner counts search feedback monthly.
claims.source_hint: ADR 0030 @ stage-4 lines 52-54; product-search-design-review.md risks table row 'Khách gõ sai nhiều hơn dự tính'

claims.text: A separate search engine (ADR 0030 option 3, design review line 68-69): richer matching and own capacity, but a copy of the products fed from Catalog's changes through the outbox, lagging behind products, needing a way to be rebuilt, one more service; 'not needed yet at the estimated size'.
claims.source_hint: ADR 0030 @ stage-4 lines 25-28; product-search-design-review.md @ stage-4 lines 68-69

claims.text: Each search takes a place in catalog-reads (20 running, 5 waiting per process), a limit on product reads, not orders; it is reached first and returns 503 for product reads, not order placement. Search is not built at stage-4.
claims.source_hint: product-search-design-review.md @ stage-4 lines 60-62; ADR 0030 line 8; DonHang.Api/Program.cs AddConcurrencyLimiter catalog-reads; OrdersController uses only the 'orders' limiter

claims.text: ADR 0016 adds a per-shop cap (assumed a quarter of 20) on top of the shared limit so one busy shop cannot fill catalog-reads; it needs the shop from the access token, from release 2, so Program.cs is unchanged at stage-4.
claims.source_hint: docs/adr/0016-gioi-han-tai-theo-cua-hang.md @ stage-4, Quyết định and Hệ quả

claims.text: capacity-plan.md moves the product list to the replica when its peak exceeds the primary's headroom, as it accepts slightly old data; consistency-per-operation.md lets search be as stale as the list (minutes, assumed) and use the replica when the plan allows.
claims.source_hint: docs/design/capacity-plan.md @ stage-4 'Đọc từ replica'; docs/design/consistency-per-operation.md @ stage-4 lines 14-15

claims.text: capacity-plan.md fallback: every read routed to the replica must return to the primary when the replica lags beyond what the product list tolerates or does not answer.
A read replica receives the primary's changes asynchronously, so a read from it may not yet see a just-committed change; PostgreSQL itself keeps it, with no feed from the team's outbox.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs 26.2.5 Streaming Replication (asynchronous by default); consistency-per-operation.md @ stage-4 lines 40-43; db/replica/start.sh (pg_basebackup)

claims.text: ProductCache keeps one product per Redis key product:{id} with a TTL of 5 minutes; its read FindAsync takes an id. The product list (CatalogService.ListAsync) queries CatalogDbContext directly, not through the cache.
claims.source_hint: DonHang.Catalog/ProductCache.cs @ stage-4 lines 18, 25-27; consistency-per-operation.md @ stage-4 line 14

claims.text: Design review trade-off point 'no cache of results by search text': assumed most searches differ, so the cache would rarely hit and adds a copy to clear on rename; caching popular searches is an open question (no measurement yet), owner the proposing team.
claims.source_hint: product-search-design-review.md @ stage-4 lines 74-75 and the last row of the challenges table

claims.text: Estimates used: at most a few thousand (review: 5,000) products per shop and about 27 searches per second at peak (20% of product reads), all assumed.

A separate search engine from the start is right when misspellings and synonyms are the driver (customers rarely know exact names) or when search load already exceeds the database's headroom; at the estimated size neither holds.
Meeting a reopen condition reopens the decision for weighing (engine with its copy, lag and rebuild path against the measured gain); it does not decide it.
claims.source_hint: ADR 0030 'Đội xem lại quyết định khi'; management.l3.superseding-an-adr
